title: Design updates for regulated workloads landing page (FinServ + Healthcare variants)
creator: Soojin Lee
description:
Goal
Update the regulated workloads landing page designs to support two vertical variants (Financial Services + Healthcare) while maximizing component reuse and meeting accessibility requirements (WCAG 2.1 AA). These designs will be implemented by ENG-2941 with HubSpot form routing and UTM attribution.

Background / context
Marketing is running a 6–8 week ABM pilot focused on regulated workloads. The landing pages need to:
- Speak to the right buyer concerns (Security/GRC + Platform/ML Engineering)
- Make the “Hosted → Dedicated → Private” deployment path feel concrete
- Provide a credible, security-forward CTA (schedule security review / request architecture review)
- Avoid over-promising; align with approved messaging and what Private/VPC supports today

Scope
1) Information architecture + copy layout (design only)
- Create two page variants:
  - /regulated/financial-services
  - /regulated/healthcare
- Shared base layout + reusable components. Vertical-specific changes should be mostly:
  - Hero headline/subhead + top proof points
  - 1–2 vertical use-case cards (FinServ: comms review, agent assist, search; Healthcare: clinical summarization/search, contact center, patient messaging)
  - Objection/FAQ module emphasis (FinServ: audit logging, KMS/HSM, tenant isolation; Healthcare: PHI assumptions, retention controls, residency)
  - Logos/testimonials section can remain generic (or removed if we don’t have vertical-safe logos)

2) Component reuse requirements
Design should reuse existing marketing components wherever possible:
- Hero (title + subhead + 2–3 bullets)
- Trust bar / “used by” strip (optional, if approved logos exist)
- 3-up feature grid
- “Deployment options” module (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with clear decision cues
- Reference architecture CTA module
- Security FAQ CTA module
- Single right-rail/sticky form (desktop) with inline form (mobile)

3) Accessibility requirements (must be explicitly checked in design)
- Color contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA (text and interactive elements)
- Visible focus states for all interactive elements (links, buttons, accordions)
- Heading structure is semantic (H1 once; then H2/H3 in order)
- Interactive accordions/FAQs designed to be keyboard navigable (clear expand/collapse affordances)
- Link styling is not color-only; underline on hover/focus at minimum
- Form fields have labels (not placeholder-only) and clear error states
- Avoid using icons as the only indicator of meaning; include text equivalents

4) Responsive behavior
- Desktop: 2-column above the fold (copy + form), sticky form begins after hero
- Tablet: form drops below hero; maintain legible line-length and spacing
- Mobile: single column; CTA buttons full-width; accordions sized for touch targets

Deliverables
- Figma frames (desktop/tablet/mobile) for both vertical variants
- Component inventory (what’s reused vs. new)
- A11y checklist notes in Figma (contrast, focus, headings, form states)
- Handoff notes for ENG-2941 (spacing tokens, component names, hover/focus states)

Open questions
- Do we want a single template with a “vertical selector” toggle, or two separate pages?
  - Recommendation: two separate pages for ABM/SEO/UTM clarity; keep components identical to limit engineering variance.
- Logos/testimonials: do we have approval to show any regulated customer logos on these pages? If not, remove the logo bar and rely on security posture + architecture proof.

Links
- Figma file: https://figma.com/file/RI-Regulated-Landing/DES-211 (internal)
- Approved messaging guardrails (Confluence): vertical-abm-regulated-workloads-core-messaging
- Security FAQ addenda (Confluence): abm-finserv-security-faq-addendum / abm-healthcare-security-faq-addendum
- Reference architecture (Confluence): private-vpc-reference-architecture-regulated-workloads

Acceptance criteria
- Two variants produced with shared component structure and minimal new components
- Meets accessibility checklist above (documented in Figma)
- Clear CTAs: “Schedule a security review” + “Request Private/VPC reference architecture” (or equivalent)
- Deployment options module makes Dedicated vs Private decision points explicit
- Design handoff is sufficient for ENG-2941 to implement without rework (states + responsive behaviors included)
comments: 2026-01-12 (Soojin Lee): Kicking off DES-211. Key requirement from #marketing: keep it security-forward and don’t imply we store/retain prompts unless phrased per approved residency/retention guidance. Prioritize a fast path to security review + architecture discussion.

2026-01-14 (Maya Patel): First wireframe pass in Figma: shared template + two variants. I kept hero + deployment module identical and swapped use-cases + FAQ emphasis. Added sticky form concept on desktop and moved “Private/VPC reference architecture” CTA above FAQs.

2026-01-16 (Ben Carter): Request: add a short “Why Redwood vs. DIY/self-hosted” strip (3 bullets) near the deployment module for performance + reliability. Also need UTM-friendly CTAs (primary button + secondary text link).

2026-01-17 (Maya Patel): Added “Operational proof points” strip (SLOs, audit logging/export, KMS integration points) but kept wording generic so Security can approve. Added explicit hover/focus styles and checked contrast on CTA buttons and secondary links.

2026-01-20 (Olga Petrov): Reviewed design/copy placement. Please ensure FAQ accordion design supports keyboard navigation and that we don’t use lock/shield icons without text. Also: avoid “HIPAA compliant” phrasing; use “supports HIPAA-aligned controls” per guidance.

2026-01-21 (Maya Patel): Updated Healthcare variant to remove any “HIPAA compliant” language in headings and used neutral module titles (“PHI considerations”, “Retention & auditability”). Added form error-state mock and helper text pattern for required fields.

2026-01-22 (Markus Klein): From SE perspective, the deployment options module should explicitly call out what customers manage in Private (networking, SIEM destination, keys) vs what Redwood manages. Even 3–4 bullets is enough to prevent confusion in discovery.

2026-01-23 (Maya Patel): Added “Shared responsibility” mini-table under Private card (high-level, non-contractual) and linked the reference architecture CTA right below. Marked as ‘overview’ with a note to defer details to the architecture doc.
2026-01-24 (Maya Patel): Finalized and ready for eng handoff. Components annotated with tokens and states; mobile/tablet frames complete. Passing to ENG-2941 for implementation.
